newsitem.title: USA: PP&L Susquehanna nuke seen restarting Fri.
newsitem.headline: PP&L Susquehanna nuke seen restarting Fri.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power and Light's 1,090 megawatt Susquehanna 1 nuclear unit was still off line early Thursday due to a valve problem and expected to restart Friday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The unit, in Berwick, Pa., was in cold shutdown, and plant operators were "troubleshooting the EHC system," the NRC report stated.
The unit was manually shut Feb 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in the unit's main condenser, which removes heat from steam leaving the unit's main turbine.
The unit was in startup mode early Tuesday following repairs to the main condenser. Startup operations were terminated shortly thereafter.
The adjacent unit 2, with a generating capacity of 1,094 MW, is scheduled to shut March 15 for refueling.
